body:
When two items move together into the same target and one of them carries `use path::Thing;` while the other *is* an item named `Thing`, extract writes both into the target. Cargo rejects the duplicate name and the whole extract rolls back.

Cause: `extract::rust.carry_imports` seeds its taken-names set from `target_names(..., |_, s| s.module == target)`, so it only sees what is already in the target, not the items arriving with the move.

Fix: seed the names from the post-move view (`extract::rust.target_names_after_move`), so a carried import that clashes with a moved item is aliased and its mentions renamed, the same way a clash with a target-local name is handled today. This also covers `carry_test_imports`, which calls the same function.

Test: `a.make` returns `std::collections::HashMap`, `b.HashMap` is a struct, and both move to a new module `w`. Assert the target has `use std::collections::HashMap as HashMap_2;` and `make` uses `HashMap_2`. It should fail (rollback) before the fix and pass after.
title: extract: carried import vs moved name clash
